title: CBSE CLASS 10 — Social Science | Federalism Centre State Relations
description: Subject-wise test on Federalism Centre State Relations (Social Science) for CBSE CLASS 10. 25Q.
subject: cbse10-sst

questions.question: Which one of the following subjects is included in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Agriculture
options.explanation: Agriculture falls under the State List or Concurrent List.

options.text: Public order
options.explanation: Public order falls under the State List.

options.text: Defence
options.explanation: Defence is listed in the Union List (Entry 1), meaning it is under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Central Government.

options.text: Trade and commerce within a state
options.explanation: Trade and commerce within a state falls under the State List or Concurrent List.

questions.explanation: Defence is listed in the Union List (Entry 1), meaning it is under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Central Government.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the principle of federalism in India?

options.text: The Central Government can abolish state governments unilaterally
options.explanation: This statement does not align with the federal structure of India.

options.text: States have the power to secede from the Union if they wish
options.explanation: This statement does not align with the federal structure of India.

options.text: The Constitution clearly demarcates powers between the Centre and the States
options.explanation: The principle of federalism in India is characterized by a clear division of powers between the Union and the States as outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.

options.text: The President of India can dismiss the Prime Minister without consulting Parliament
options.explanation: This statement does not align with the federal structure of India.

questions.explanation: The principle of federalism in India is characterized by a clear division of powers between the Union and the States as outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.question: Read the following statements about Cooperative Federalism in India: I. It emphasizes a strong Centre with limited autonomy for States. II. It allows States to frame their own economic policies without any Central interference. Which of the above statements are correct?

options.text: I and II only
options.explanation: Statement I is incorrect.

options.text: II and III only
options.explanation: Cooperative federalism involves State participation and institutions like the Inter-State Council.

options.text: II and III only
options.explanation: Cooperative federalism involves State participation and institutions like the Inter-State Council.

options.text: I, II, and III
options.explanation: Statement I is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Cooperative federalism involves State participation and institutions like the Inter-State Council.

questions.question: In the context of Centre-State financial relations, which of the following is not a function of the Finance Commission?

options.text: Distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Centre and States.
options.explanation: The Finance Commission does recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes.

options.text: Recommendation of grants-in-aid to States from the Consolidated Fund of India.
options.explanation: The Finance Commission does recommend grants-in-aid to States.

options.text: Directly levying taxes on certain commodities to reduce fiscal imbalance.
options.explanation: The Finance Commission does not levy taxes directly.
